headline: Futures bounce from Friday's AI rout, but the crack hasn't fully healed
body: Monday's open looks like relief rather than resolution. Nasdaq 100 futures were up roughly 1%-plus and S&P 500 futures around 0.5%-0.7% in premarket trading, clawing back a slice of Friday's tech-led selloff that left the Nasdaq down about 4.5% on the week, its worst since June. The names at the center of Friday's damage are leading the bounce: Broadcom and Nvidia both rose in premarket trade, and CoreWeave, which fell nearly 12% Friday after its credit-default-swap spreads hit record highs, was higher too. That pattern (the most-hit names snapping back hardest) is more consistent with short-covering and dip-buying in a crowded trade than with the underlying worry being resolved. The 10-year yield easing toward the low 5% area and Brent crude dropping roughly 2% after Washington eased some Russia sanctions are modest tailwinds, but the core question from last week, whether AI-infrastructure spending is outrunning the financing and cash flow backing it, is still open.

The next real test is earnings, not price action: Tesla and Meta report Wednesday, with GM, Netflix, RTX, and several industrials also due this week, and strategists are split on whether results can validate the AI capex story or add to the skepticism that hit chip and software names. Positioning chatter is thin again today; broad social and retail-sentiment searches turned up little specific or current signal, so this read leans on futures action, credit-spread and yield moves, and the earnings calendar rather than crowd mood. On balance it reads as a market trying to stabilize after a sharp, narrow unwind, with conviction likely to hinge on what Big Tech says about spending and returns later this week rather than on anything resolved this morning.
